 1                       I.    WITNESS IDENTIFICATION

 2   Q.   Please state your name and business address.

 3   A.   My name is Allison M. Johnson. My business address is 3500 Blake Street, Denver,

 4        Colorado 80205.

 5   Q.   On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

 6   A.   I am filing testimony on behalf of Southwestern Public Service Company, a New

 7        Mexico corporation (“SPS”) and wholly-owned electric utility subsidiary of Xcel

8         Energy Inc.

 9   Q.   Are you the same Allison M. Johnson who filed direct testimony on behalf of

10        SPS in this case?

11   A.   Yes.

 1             II.    ASSIGNMENT AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY

 2   Q.   What is your assignment in this testimony?

 3   A.   I am providing testimony in support of Section I of the Comprehensive Stipulation

 4        (“Stipulation”), specifically Section 1.1 – Agreement as to Base Rate Increase,

 5        Section 1.4 – Interim Recovery of BESS Long-Term Purchased Power Agreement

 6        Costs, Section 1.5 – SPS Short-Term Capacity Needs, Section 1.8 – Treatment of

 7        Federal Tax Credits and Section 1.17 – Jurisdictional Allocation. I am also

 8        providing testimony that demonstrates the Stipulation meets the criteria the New

 9        Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”) has established for

10        reviewing the reasonableness of a settlement.

11   Q.   Please summarize your testimony and overall recommendations.

12   A.   I recommend the Commission approve the Stipulation as it represents a reasonable

13        compromise of the Signatories, provides New Mexico customers with a number of

14        benefits compared to a fully litigated outcome, and is in the public interest. In my

15        testimony, I discuss various perspectives in reviewing the Stipulation that

16        demonstrate its benefits. Further, I specifically discuss how Sections 1.4, 1.5, 1.8

17        and 1.17 are in the public interest and are consistent with standard ratemaking




                                               2
                              Case No. 25-00079-UT
                             Testimony in Support of
                            Comprehensive Stipulation
                                       of
                               Allison M. Johnson

1   practice. Finally, I describe the reconciliation statement attached to the Stipulation

2   as Exhibit D.

1            III.       COMMISSION ESTABLISHED CRITERIA FOR
2                            REVIEWING SETTLEMENTS

 3   Q.   What are the criteria the Commission has established to review a settlement?

 4   A.   As discussed in more detail by SPS witness Ms. Zoë E. Lees, the Commission has

 5        established the following criteria for reviewing the reasonableness of a stipulation:

 6            (1)     Is the settlement a product of serious bargaining among capable,
 7                    knowledgeable parties?

8             (2)     Does the settlement, as a whole, benefit customers and the public
9                     interest?

10            (3)     Does the settlement, as a whole, violate any important regulatory
11                    principle or practice?

12   Q.   Does the Stipulation satisfy these three criteria?

13   A.   Yes. Ms. Lees discusses the first criterion in her testimony. In my testimony, I

14        explain how the sections of the Stipulation I support meet items (2) and (3) of the

15        criteria.




                                               4
                                       Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                      Testimony in Support of
                                     Comprehensive Stipulation

                                        Allison M. Johnson

1         IV.          THE STIPULATION, AS A WHOLE, BENEFITS SPS’S
2                       CUSTOMERS AND IS IN THE PUBLIC INTEREST

3         A.        Section 1.1 to the Stipulation—Base Rate Revenue Increase

4    Q.   Please describe Section 1.1 of the Stipulation.

5    A.   Section 1.1 of the Stipulation addresses the base rate revenue increase and the

 6        specific number of cost of service components the Signatories agreed to. Ms. Lees

 7        discusses the Stipulation and Section 1.1 in more detail, but for the purposes of my

 8        testimony, the main aspects of the agreement include: (1) a base rate increase of

 9        $90 million; (2) a revised 12-coincident peak (“12CP-PROD”) allocator reflecting

10        the removal of associated New Mexico loads, to coincide with the direct assignment

11        of Cunningham Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”) costs and capacity to

12        New Mexico Retail; (3) the removal of both BESS long-term Purchased Power

13        Agreement (“LTPPA) and Southwest Power Pool (“SPP”) deficiency payments

14        from the cost of service; and (4) the treatment of federal production tax credits

15        (“PTC”) and investment tax credits (“ITC”).

16                  I have also incorporated the following revisions into the cost of service from

17        other SPS witness testimony:

18              •    revised return on equity (“ROE”) of 9.50%, as discussed by SPS witness
19                   Ms. Ann E. Bulkley,

                                                  5
                                      Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                     Testimony in Support of
                                    Comprehensive Stipulation
                                               of
                                       Allison M. Johnson

 1             •      a revised capital structure consisting of 54.7% common equity and 45.3%
 2                    long-term debt, as discussed by SPS witness Mr. Todd A. Wehner,

 3             •      a revised 12CP-PROD jurisdictional allocator, as discussed by SPS
 4                    witness Mr. Taylor J. Hurt,

5              •      revised depreciation expense, as discussed by SPS witness Ms. Michele
6                     A. Kietzman,

7              •      a three-year amortization of deferred Excess Liability Insurance (“ELI”)
8                     costs, as discussed by SPS witness Ms. Lees

 9             •      a four-year amortization of remaining legacy meter balances, as discussed
10                    by SPS witness Ms. Lees

11             •      a four-year amortization of Community Solar Program costs, as discussed
12                    by SPS witness Ms..Lees, and

13             •      a two-year amortization of rate case expenses, as discussed by SPS
14                    witness Ms. Lees.

15                 Finally, I have included Attachments AMJ-STIP-1 and AMJ-STIP-2, which

16        detail the revenue requirement associated with the Hale and Sagamore Wind

17        Projects.

18   Q.   Are there different ways to review the stipulated revenue requirement that

19        indicate its reasonableness?

20   A.   The Stipulation specifies the $90 million increase “is not associated with any

21        specific calculation involving any of the stated cost of service components [in the

22        Stipulation], or approval or disapproval of any other issue raised in this case,” and

                                                 6
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1        it reflects “a compromise of the various issues raised in this case without

 2        specifically accepting or rejecting for purposes of this Stipulation any ratemaking

 3        issue or principle other than those specified [in the Stipulation].” There are,

 4        however, various ways of looking at the agreed base rate increase that demonstrate

 5        its reasonableness.

 6   Q.   Please discuss the ways of looking at the Stipulation that demonstrate it is

 7        reasonable and in the public interest.

 8   A.   One way to review the Stipulation, which Ms. Lees discusses, is to compare it to

 9        SPS’s request. Another way, which I discuss below, is to review how the

10        Stipulation addresses the primary drivers of SPS’s revenue requirement and

11        requested increase.

12   Q.   What were the primary drivers of SPS’s requested non-fuel base rate

13        increase?

14   A.   There were three primary categories of cost drivers of SPS’s requested non-fuel

15        base rate increase: (1) changes in jurisdictional allocations; (2) retail load growth

16        and the related investment to serve SPS’s customers; and (3) operations and

17        maintenance (“O&M”) expense and regulatory amortizations associated with

                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                    Testimony in Support of
                                   Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                      Allison M. Johnson

 1        previously-approved regulatory assets and deferrals. The table below presents the

 2        main cost drivers in more detail.

 4   Q.   What does Table AMJ-STIP-1 show?

 5   A.   The above table shows the major components of SPS’s revenue requirement that

 6        have changed relative to the revenue requirement established in Case No.

 7        22-00286-UT.     As shown in the table, SPS has experienced additional costs

 8        associated with allocator changes for load growth and the declining wholesale

 9        loads, in addition to base rate revenue growth, which offsets these trends. The base

10        rate increase reflected in the Stipulation addresses these allocation changes, but also

11        the new plant investment necessary for servicing SPS’s customers while at the same

12        time advancing the Commission’s renewable energy goals. It also includes known




                                                8
                                   Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                  Testimony in Support of
                                 Comprehensive Stipulation
                                            of
                                    Allison M. Johnson

1         increases necessary for establishing O&M at appropriate levels, together with

2         regulatory amortizations associated with hazard insurance and legacy meters.

3    Q.   Please describe the treatment of cash working capital in the Stipulation.

4    A.   The Signatories agreed that the base rate increase reflects a cash working capital

5         balance of $0. SPS’s original request included a cash working capital balance of

6         $74,454,952 total company ($34,605,261 NM retail) based on the 1/8th method

7         discussed in Ms. Lees’s direct testimony. The use of a cash working capital balance

 8        of $0 is consistent with the recommendations from New Mexico Large Customer

 9        Group (“NMLCG”) witness Ms. Celia B. Hashlamoun and Federal Executive

10        Agencies, Louisiana Energy Services, LLC (“LES-FEA”) witness Mr. James A.

11        Leyko. Further, it represents a compromise among the Signatories and results in a

12        decrease of $3,464,502 to SPS’s revenue requirement and the rates charged to

13        customers.

14   Q.   Is Section 1.1 of the Stipulation beneficial to SPS’s customers and in the public

15        interest?

16   A.   Yes, for the reasons explained by Ms. Lees in her Testimony in Support of the

17        Comprehensive Stipulation.

 1   Q.   Does Section 1.1 of the Stipulation violate any important regulatory principle

 2        or practice?

 3   A.   No. Section 1.1 of the Stipulation is consistent with existing regulatory principles

 4        and practices and does not request any exception from any Commission rule or

 5        practice.

 6        B.     Section 1.4 to the Stipulation—Interim Recovery of BESS
 7               Long-Term Purchased Power Agreement Costs
 8   Q.   Please describe Section 1.4 of the Stipulation.

 9   A.   The Signatories agreed that SPS withdraw its request to recover through its Fuel

10        and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment Clause (“FPPCAC”) the capacity costs for

11        BESS long-term purchased power agreements. These costs were approved in Case

12        No. 25-00085. SPS included these costs in its direct filing but has removed them

13        from the cost of service as part of the stipulation. This recommendation is

14        consistent with the proposal by NMLCG witness Ms. Hashlamoun.

15               Within its Comprehensive List of Revisions, SPS removed the costs for

16        Panhandle BESS from its cost of service to reflect the postponement of this

17        agreement outside the Future Test Year. In Stipulation, SPS is removing all



                                              10
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1        remaining BESS long-term Purchased Power agreements, which reduces the

 2        revenue requirement an additional $9,635,593.

 3   Q.   Is Section 1.4 of the Stipulation beneficial to SPS’s customers and in the public

 4        interest?

5    A.   Yes. The removal of BESS long-term purchased power capacity costs represents a

6         compromise among the Signatories and results in a decrease to SPS’s revenue

7         requirement and the rates charged to customers. SPS reserves the right to seek

8         recovery of these costs through an alternative cost recovery mechanism, such as the

9         FPPCAC, in a future proceeding.

10   Q.   Does Section 1.4 of the Stipulation violate any important regulatory principle

11        or practice?

12   A.   No. Section 1.4 of the Stipulation is consistent with existing regulatory principles

13        and practices and does not request any exception from any Commission rule or

14        practice.

 1        C.      Section 1.5 to the Stipulation—SPS Short-Term Capacity
 2                Needs
 3   Q.   Please describe Section 1.5 of the Stipulation.

 4   A.   The Signatories agreed that SPS withdraw its request, without prejudice, to recover

 5        through its FPPCAC any deficiency payments to Southwest Power Pool. SPS

 6        included these costs in its direct filing but has removed them from the cost of

 7        service as part of the stipulation, which constitutes a reduction of $4,907,322 to the

 8        revenue requirement.     This recommendation is consistent with proposals by

 9        NMLCG witness Ms. Hashlamoun, LES-FEA witness Mr. Leyko, Utility Division

10        Staff (“STAFF”) witness Mr. Jonah B. Mauldin, and Occidental Permian Ltd.

11        (“OPL”) witness Ms. Billie S. LaConte. As discussed in Ms. Lees’s testimony, SPS

12        will use its best efforts to address short-term capacity needs, including, where

13        prudent, pursuing short-term capacity purchases in lieu of making Southwest Power

14        Pool deficiency payments. SPS will defer and record as a regulatory asset any such

15        short-term capacity purchases or deficiency payments incurred through the

16        effective date of new rates and seek recovery of these costs through a future

17        proceeding, subject to an annual cap of $10 million for the New Mexico retail

18        jurisdiction.

                                               12
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1   Q.   Is Section 1.5 of the Stipulation beneficial to SPS’s customers and in the public

 2        interest?

 3   A.   Yes. The removal of SPP deficiency payments represents a compromise among the

 4        Signatories and results in a decrease to SPS’s revenue requirement and the rates

 5        charged to customers. SPS may seek recovery of these deferred costs through a

 6        future proceeding.

 7   Q.   Does Section 1.5 of the Stipulation violate any important regulatory principle

 8        or practice?

 9   A.   No. Section 1.5 of the Stipulation is consistent with existing regulatory principles

10        and practices and does not request any exception from any Commission rule or

11        practice.

12        D.     Section 1.8 to the Stipulation—Treatment of Federal Tax
13               Credits
14   Q.   Please describe Section 1.8 of the Stipulation.

15   A.   There are three components to this section. In Section A, Production Tax Credits

16        for SPS Solar Projects, the Signatories agreed that SPS may earn a return on its

17        Solar Deferred Tax Asset (“DTA”) for production tax credits created by Plant X

18        Solar, Cunningham I Solar and Cunningham II Solar at its long-term cost of debt


                                              13
                               Case No. 25-00079-UT
                              Testimony in Support of
                             Comprehensive Stipulation
                                        of
                                Allison M. Johnson

 1   through the FPPCAC. Accordingly, SPS has removed from rate base the value of

 2   these deferred tax assets, and the associated return.

 3          In Section B, Investment Tax Credits for Cunningham BESS and Plant X

 4   BESS, the Signatories agreed that SPS is authorized to amortize its investment tax

 5   credits (“ITCs”) for Cunningham BESS and Plant X BESS over five years. The

 6   Cunningham BESS ITC amortization will begin in December 2026 in alignment

 7   with new rates, and the Plant X BESS ITC amortization will begin upon the Plant

 8   X BESS commercial operation date. SPS shall amortize Cunningham BESS

 9   transfer costs, capped at 10% of the corresponding ITCs’ nominal value, over the

10   same amortization period as the ITC value. Further, SPS is authorized to accrue a

11   regulatory asset for Plant X BESS transfer costs subject to a 10% cap of the ITC’s

12   nominal value.

13          Section C, PTC Transfer Costs for Hale and Sagamore stipulates that SPS

14   may recover Hale and Sagamore Wind Project transfer costs, capped at 10% of

15   nominal value, through SPS’s FPPCAC.

16          Of the aforementioned sections, only Section A constitutes a direct change

17   to the cost of service. As part of the Stipulation, SPS has removed the New Mexico


                                          14
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1        retail portion of the Solar PTC DTA, totaling $5,770,468, from rate base, thereby

 2        reducing the revenue requirement by $571,936.

 3   Q.   Is Section 1.8 of the Stipulation beneficial to SPS’s customers and in the public

 4        interest?

 5   A.   Yes. The removal of solar PTC DTA from rate base represents a compromise

 6        among the Signatories and results in a decrease to SPS’s revenue requirement and

 7        the rates charged to customers. SPS maintains an avenue for recovery of these costs

 8        through FFPAC.

 9   Q.   Does Section 1.8 of the Stipulation violate any important regulatory principle

10        or practice?

11   A.   No. Section 1.8 of the Stipulation is consistent with existing regulatory principles

12        and practices and does not request any exception from any Commission rule or

13        practice.

14        E.     Section 1.17 to the Stipulation—Jurisdictional Allocation

15   Q.   Please describe Section 1.17 of the Stipulation.

16   A.   Within Section 1.3 of the Stipulation, the Signatories agreed that SPS direct assign

17        all costs and capacity benefits associated with Cunningham BESS to New Mexico

18        retail customers. Section 1.17 complements this section. SPS agrees to adjust its
                                              15
                                    Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                   Testimony in Support of
                                  Comprehensive Stipulation
                                             of
                                     Allison M. Johnson

 1        12CP-PROD production jurisdictional system allocators by removing New Mexico

 2        loads for Cunningham BESS from the shared system capacity. This allows for a

 3        better alignment of jurisdictional allocators, costs and benefits, as explained by SPS

 4        witness Mr. Hurt. This recommendation is consistent with the proposal by Staff

 5        witness Mr. Larry Blank..

 6               In Stipulation Section 1.17, SPS is using a modified 12CP-PROD allocator

 7        that achieves this recommendation. This revised allocator lowers the New Mexico

 8        retail revenue requirement by $1,437,157.

 9   Q.   Is Section 1.17 of the Stipulation beneficial to SPS’s customers and in the

10        public interest?

11   A.   Yes.   The removal of New Mexico Cunningham BESS loads represents a

12        compromise among the Signatories and results in a decrease to SPS’s revenue

13        requirement and the rates charged to customers.

14   Q.   Does Section 1.17 of the Stipulation violate any important regulatory principle

15        or practice?

16   A.   No. Section 1.17 of the Stipulation is consistent with existing regulatory principles

17        and practices and does not request any exception from any Commission rule or

18        practice.

1         F.         Exhibit D to the Stipulation—Reconciliation Statement

2    Q.   What is a reconciliation statement?

3    A.   The reconciliation statement is required by Commission Rule 1.2.2.20.A(2) and is

4         to contain the following information as stated in Commission Rule 1.2.2.36.F:

5              (a)    the claimed rate base for the regulated entity showing test year figures per
6                     book, adjustments, and adjusted test year figures (if rate base items are at
7                     issue the statement shall set forth on a separate sheet the contested items
8                     and their dollar effect on rate base);
 9             (b)    an income statement showing operating revenues and expenses with test
10                    year figures per book, adjustments, and adjusted test year figures (if any
11                    expense items are at issue the statement shall set forth on a separate sheet
12                    the contested expense or revenue items in detail and the dollar effect on
13                    total company expenses or revenues of their allowance);
14             (c)    the capital structure of the company (if there is no actual capital structure,
15                    any proposed imputed capital structure, the ratio of each type of capital to
16                    total capital, and the cost and weighted cost of each shall be shown; this
17                    schedule shall show the dollar effects of the requested return upon revenue
18                    requirements);
19             (d)    a computation of projected state and federal taxes on adjusted figures
20                    based on statutory rates or other applicable rates; and
21             (e)    a computation of the claimed revenue deficiency.
22   Q.   Has SPS included a reconciliation statement in support of the Stipulation?

23   A.   Yes. SPS prepared a reconciliation statement and it is included as Exhibit D to the

24        Stipulation.

 1   Q.   Please describe the reconciliation statement.

 2   A.   The reconciliation statement is a seven-page document summarizing the revenue

 3        request in the Stipulation. Pages 1-3 show the income statement components of the

 4        revenue requirement starting from per book amounts and showing the adjustments

 5        to arrive at the adjusted Future Test Year amounts. Pages 4-5 present the same

 6        information for the components of rate base. The income statement and rate base

 7        information is presented on both a total SPS and New Mexico retail basis. Pages

 8        6-7 present the calculation of the revenue deficiency. This reconciliation statement

 9        shows all of the items required by (a) through (e) above.

10   Q.   Does this conclude your pre-filed testimony in support of the Stipulation?

11   A.   Yes.
